    Ground Truth Content:
     With large speech corpora and the development of sequence-to-sequence models, recent text-to-speech(TTS) models have achieved human-like speech synthesis at a level comparable to human speech utterances #ref1# #ref2# #ref3#. Multi-speaker TTS can synthesize speech with the desired speaker characteristics by inputting speaker information in addition to text #ref4# #ref5# #ref6#. TTS training typically requires pairs of text and speech. The speech data is recorded in a well-designed environment #ref7# #ref8# #ref9#, e.g., a recording studio with a professional speaker. Furthermore, constructing a multi-speaker TTS corpus is even more burdensome. This fact significantly limits the variety of speakers that TTS can synthesize. Fig.1 is an example of speaker distributions of a famous multi-speaker TTS corpus (JVS #ref9#) and one we deal with in this paper. This is a t-SNE #ref10# plot of #eq0#-vectors #ref11# of natural speech in the two corpora. Typical multi-speaker TTS corpora only cover limited speaker variation. In contrast, there is a large amount of speech data (e.g., YouTube videos) with unknown potential for machine learning, known as dark data #ref12# #ref13#, on the Internet. We expect to solve the small speaker variation problem if we can fully automate TTS model training from dark data. Related to this, methods have been proposed for building TTS corpora from datasets other than TTS corpora #ref14# #ref15# #ref16# #ref17#. These methods determine a TTS corpus on the basis of the acoustic quality of each utterance. On the other hand, recent TTS models are becoming more robust to data noise than the old-fashioned parametric models #ref18# #ref19# #ref20#. In other words, low-quality speech data does not necessarily have a negative impact on TTS model training. In light of the above, TTS corpus construction should be based on the importance of the speech data as training data for a given TTS model, not on the quality of speech data itself. This paper proposes an evaluation-in-the-loop data selection method for TTS model training from dark data. Our method uses a pseudo score on the perceptual quality of synthetic speech output from a given TTS model and scores each of the training data candidates in terms of the importance of training data rather than acoustic quality. The training data candidates are filtered by the importance. The procedure automates the selection and training loop using a pre-trained model that automatically predicts the mean opinion score(MOS) of synthetic speech on naturalness. This paper also proposes a method for pre-screening dark data for TTS use, achieving a fully automated process from dark data collection to TTS model training. We conduct experiments with dark data, in particular, actual data obtained from YouTube. The results show that our evaluation-in-the-loop method achieves better than the conventional acoustic-quality-based method. The contributions of this work are as follows: We propose an evaluation-in-the-loop data selection method for TTS model training, that enables more efficient selection than the conventional acoustic-quality-based method. We conduct experiments using actual data downloaded from YouTube and demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

If the noise is too high, the synthetic speech quality will be degraded. Therefore, previous studies have selected dark data on the basis of acoustic quality. In #ref7#, the authors proposed an acoustic-quality-based data selection method for TTS training. The method estimates the acoustic quality of each utterance from dark data using a pre-trained acoustic quality estimator. The utterances are then ranked and selected according to their acoustic quality. In #ref8#, the authors proposed a method to select dark data by combining the acoustic quality and the confidence of the phoneme recognition result. In #ref9#, the authors proposed a method to select dark data on the basis of the distance between the acoustic features of the utterances and the feature distribution of the TTS training data. However, the TTS model can generate high-quality synthetic speech even if the noise in the speech is high. Therefore, the quality of the speech itself is not the only factor that affects the quality of the synthetic speech. It is important to select dark data on the basis of the importance of the data to the given TTS model.

In this paper, we propose a method to select dark data for TTS training on the basis of the importance of the data to the given TTS model. Our method uses a loop of training and evaluation. In the loop, we train the TTS model with the dark data selected by the data selection method and evaluate the quality of the synthetic speech generated from the trained model. The method then updates the importance of the data in the dark data on the basis of the quality of the synthetic speech. The training and evaluation are repeated until the data selection converges.

The contributions of this paper are as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item We propose a method to select training data for TTS from dark data. The method selects data on the basis of the importance of the data to the given TTS model, not the quality of the speech itself.
\item We propose an evaluation-in-the-loop data selection method. The method updates the importance of the data in the dark data on the basis of the quality of the synthetic speech.
\end{itemize}
